# The anatomy of a card

One card per skill, at `index/<name>.md`, generated by `skillhelp build` and
committed. A card is a **routing surface**, not a copy of the skill's docs: it
holds the lines worth pointing at, each with the line it came from.

```
# gmailtriage

<!-- GENERATED by @natjswenson/skillhelp — do not edit. Run `skillhelp build`. -->

- **version** — 0.4.0
- **stack** — node
- **summary** — Sort and clean a Gmail inbox… `skills/gmailtriage/skills/gmailtriage/SKILL.md:3`
- **triggers** — "clean my inbox", "gmailtriage", …

## Setup
- Node 18+ (the bundled scripts are ESM, no dependencies). `skills/gmailtriage/README.md:95`

## Usage
## Commands
## Architecture
## Troubleshooting
```

## The five sections are fixed

Always these five, always in this order, for every skill. A skill with no source
for a section gets:

```
_No source for this section in this skill's files._
```

**That line is the point.** A fixed shape means a card is never "whatever this
skill happened to document", and an empty section is a true statement about the
skill rather than a gap papered over with the nearest available prose. Padding
it is how an index starts answering questions it cannot answer.

`build` names every thin card in its output (`thin — <skill> has no source
for: architecture`), so an empty section is visible at build time, not
discovered by a user who asked.

## Every fact carries a source

A fact is one line ending in a backticked repo-relative `path:line`:

```
- Node 18+ (the bundled scripts are ESM, no dependencies). `skills/gmailtriage/README.md:95`
```

A bullet without one is a defect with its own verdict (`ungrounded`) and its own
test. Sources are **repo-relative** — never absolute — because an absolute path
encodes the machine that built the card, passes locally, and fails in CI.

## A fact is a block, not a line

Markdown here is hard-wrapped at ~80 columns. Indexing line-at-a-time produced
facts like *"Two things happen to mail you do not want in your inbox: some of it
should go in"* — a sentence sawn in half, cited to a line number that is
technically correct and useless. A fact is therefore a **block**: a paragraph, a
list item with its continuations, or a table row, anchored at the line it starts
on and truncated at 200 characters. The source is how you read the rest.

## Caps, and why they are low

| Section | Cap |
|---|---|
| setup | 12 |
| usage | 12 |
| commands | 20 |
| architecture | 16 |
| troubleshooting | 16 |

Past these counts an extra fact does not make the card more complete, it makes
every question asked of it noisier. If a section is at its cap the answer to
"why isn't X in the card" is nearly always "raise the source's quality", not
"raise the cap".

## Deduplication is card-wide

A line that qualifies for both Setup and Usage is indexed **once**. Showing it
twice pads the card and makes a two-section hit look like corroboration when it
is one source saying one thing.

## The hash is over the rendered card

`index/_manifest.json` stores `cardHash` — a hash of the **rendered card**, never
of the skill's file tree. Drift therefore means *the answer would change*, which
is the only kind of drift worth reddening CI over. A typo fix in a code comment
inside a skill's `scripts/` changes its tree and changes no card.

Nothing version-stamped by skillhelp itself appears in the rendered bytes. press
learned this expensively: a generator version embedded in generated output makes
every release look like a content change to every byte comparison downstream.
